logic.note: AM2302 single-bus protocol bit for bit: start pulse ≥ 0.8 ms, 80/80 µs response, 40 data bits (humidity, temperature with sign bit, checksum), open-drain line with the module's 10 kΩ pull-up. Answers with the measurement from the previous read, as the datasheet says.

timing.note: Cycle-exact on the MCU clock: response 30 µs after the release, bits of 50 µs LOW + 26 or 70 µs HIGH, so both libraries and hand-written readers that time pulses see datasheet timing. No answer in the first 1 s after power-up; reads closer than 2 s repeat the old measurement.

analog.note: Reports exactly the temperature and humidity you set (0.1 resolution). Real accuracy is ±0.5 °C and ±2–5 % RH, with slow response (~2 s for temperature, longer for humidity) and self-heating if read too often.

power.note: 50 µA standby on VCC, works from 3.0 V. The ~1.5 mA during a measurement is not modelled.

emulates: Start signal detection and the full 40-bit answer
Previous-measurement answer and the 2 s minimum interval
doesNotEmulate: Sensor accuracy, drift and response time
Long-wire capacitance (keep the wire under ~20 m with a stronger pull-up)
testOnRealDevice: Compare against a reference thermometer / hygrometer
Reads failing with long wires or without the pull-up (bare 4-pin sensor)
That firmware handles a failed read (it happens on hardware)
